questions.stem: What was the first artificial satellite launched into space?

options.text: International Space Station
Hubble Space Telescope
Sputnik 1, launched by the USSR in 1957
Apollo 11

questions.explanation: Sputnik 1, launched by the USSR in 1957, was the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth. It marked the beginning of the Space Age and was followed by rapid developments in space exploration.

questions.stem: What is a key advantage of space-based telescopes over ground-based telescopes?

options.text: They can only observe in visible light
They are above the atmosphere, so images are not distorted and they can observe wavelengths absorbed by the atmosphere
They are closer to the stars they observe
They are cheaper to build and maintain

questions.explanation: Space-based telescopes are above Earth's atmosphere, so their images are not distorted by atmospheric turbulence. They can also observe wavelengths such as infrared, ultraviolet, and X-rays that are blocked or absorbed by the atmosphere.

questions.stem: Why are robotic probes often preferred over human missions for exploring distant planets?

options.text: Robots can travel faster than humans
Robots are more intelligent than humans
They are much cheaper, carry no risk to human life, and can operate for years in extreme environments
Robotic probes are not preferred; human missions are always better

questions.explanation: Robotic probes are much cheaper (no life support needed), carry no risk to human life, can operate in extreme environments, and can last many years. However, humans offer greater flexibility and problem-solving ability for complex tasks.

questions.stem: Why is communication delay a significant problem when controlling a rover on Mars?

options.text: Mars is too far for any signals to reach
Signals take at least 4 minutes each way, making real-time control impossible
Radio signals cannot travel through space
Mars has no atmosphere to carry radio signals

questions.explanation: Radio signals take at least 4 minutes to travel from Earth to Mars (and up to 24 minutes depending on orbital positions), with the same delay for the return. This minimum 8-minute round trip makes real-time control impossible, so rovers must have autonomous navigation capabilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a physical challenge faced during human spaceflight?

options.text: Space is too bright for astronauts to see
Muscle and bone loss due to microgravity
Excessive gravity
Too much oxygen in space

questions.explanation: In microgravity, astronauts experience muscle atrophy and bone density loss because their bodies do not need to work against gravity. Regular exercise is required on the ISS to counteract these effects during long-duration missions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a technology spinoff from space exploration?

options.text: Petrol-powered cars
Steam engines
Coal-fired power stations
Water purification systems and memory foam

questions.explanation: Water purification technology developed for spacecraft is now used in clean water systems on Earth, and memory foam was originally developed for NASA aircraft seats. Other spinoffs include scratch-resistant lenses and medical imaging improvements.

questions.stem: What is the International Space Station (ISS) primarily used for?

options.text: An international research laboratory for microgravity experiments, medical research, and technology testing
A refuelling station for missions to Mars
Mining asteroids
A military base in orbit

questions.explanation: The ISS is an international research laboratory orbiting at about 400 km altitude. It is used for microgravity experiments, medical research on the effects of spaceflight, materials science, and testing technologies for future deep-space missions.
